note: Hand-derived expected values for ADR-0001 revision 2; see README.md and tools/derive_fixtures.py. runs: [db, n] finite frames, [db, n, 'clipped'], [null, n] non-finite, ['gap', n] missing frames. 50 ms frames; 48 kHz timing (t_audio_ms = frame_index * 50). Not measurements of any real microphone.

cases.description: Typical quiet room, all rules satisfied.
cases.derivation: Blocks of 100 frames: sorted indices 0-19 = A, 20-49 = B, 50-79 = C, 80-94 = D, 95-99 = E. Nearest rank for n = 100: p20 = sorted[19] = A, floor = p50 = sorted[49] = B, p80 = sorted[79] = C, p95 = sorted[94] = D. Emitted values are rounded to 0.1 dB (Math.round, ties toward +infinity) and the dB rules are decided on the emitted values. p80 - p20 = -40 - (-46) = 6 (<= 6, stable). p95 - floor = -36 - (-43) = 7 (<= 10). floor -43 <= -30 and >= -110. Coverage 100/100 = 1. Valid.

cases.description: Stability boundary: p80 - p20 = 6.1 dB (the finest step on the 0.1 dB grid above the limit).

cases.description: Raw p80 - p20 = 6.04 dB: the emitted p80 is -44.0, the rule is decided on emitted values, so the quiet check is valid.
cases.derivation: Blocks of 100 frames: sorted indices 0-19 = A, 20-49 = B, 50-79 = C, 80-94 = D, 95-99 = E. cases.description: Loudness boundary: floor is exactly -30.0 dBFS.
cases.derivation: Blocks of 100 frames: sorted indices 0-19 = A, 20-49 = B, 50-79 = C, 80-94 = D, 95-99 = E. Nearest rank for n = 100: p20 = sorted[19] = A, floor = p50 = sorted[49] = B, p80 = sorted[79] = C, p95 = sorted[94] = D. Emitted values are rounded to 0.1 dB (Math.round, ties toward +infinity) and the dB rules are decided on the emitted values. floor = -30 <= -30: valid. p80 - p20 = -28 - (-33) = 5. p95 - floor = -24 - (-30) = 6.

cases.description: Loudness boundary: floor is -29.9 dBFS.
cases.derivation: Blocks of 100 frames: sorted indices 0-19 = A, 20-49 = B, 50-79 = C, 80-94 = D, 95-99 = E. cases.description: Raw floor -29.96 dBFS rounds to -30.0 and is not too loud.
cases.derivation: Blocks of 100 frames: sorted indices 0-19 = A, 20-49 = B, 50-79 = C, 80-94 = D, 95-99 = E. cases.description: Coverage boundary: 90 of 100 expected frames.
cases.derivation: 90 finite frames at -50 dBFS, expected_frames = 5000/50 = 100: coverage 90/100 = 0.90 >= 0.90. All percentiles are -50. Valid.

cases.description: Coverage boundary: 89 of 100 expected frames.
cases.derivation: 89 finite frames, expected 100: coverage 0.89 < 0.90: low_coverage.

cases.description: One clipped frame invalidates and is excluded from the statistics.
cases.derivation: 99 finite non-clipped frames at -50 plus 1 clipped frame at -3. Statistics use the 99 non-clipped frames only, so every percentile is -50. Coverage counts finite frames: 100/100. clipped_frames = 1 > 0: clipped.

cases.description: 5 of 100 frames non-finite is not more than 5 %.
cases.derivation: 95 finite frames at -50 and 5 non-finite. Non-finite fraction 5/100 = 0.05, not > 0.05. Coverage 95/100 = 0.95 >= 0.90: valid. Non-finite frames are excluded from statistics.

cases.description: 6 of 100 frames non-finite is more than 5 %.
cases.derivation: 94 finite + 6 non-finite: non-finite fraction 0.06 > 0.05: nonfinite (evaluated before coverage, which would pass at 0.94).

cases.description: Revision 2 priority: nonfinite is evaluated before low_coverage.
cases.derivation: 40 finite + 10 non-finite = 50 frames received of 100 expected. Non-finite fraction 10/50 = 0.2 > 0.05 -> nonfinite. Coverage 40/100 = 0.4 < 0.90 would be low_coverage, but nonfinite has priority (A1-07).

cases.description: A1-05: floor exactly -110.0 dBFS is not silent_input.
cases.derivation: floor = -110.0, not < -110: valid. Stability, burst and loudness rules hold (all percentiles equal).

cases.description: A1-05: floor -110.1 dBFS is silent_input.
cases.derivation: floor = -110.1 < -110: silent_input (the phone microphone looks muted or blocked).

cases.description: A1-05: digital silence (-140 dBFS) used to pass the quiet check and is now silent_input.
cases.derivation: 100 frames at -140 dBFS: p80 - p20 = 0 and floor <= -30 (the revision 1 rules passed), but floor -140 < -110: silent_input.

cases.description: Raw floor -110.04 rounds to -110.0: not silent.
Raw floor -110.06 rounds to -110.1: silent.
A1-05 applies to the pre-window check too.
cases.derivation: 40 frames at -140: floor -140 < -110: silent_input (pre_window reason set includes silent_input).

cases.description: low_coverage is evaluated before silent_input.
cases.derivation: 50 of 100 frames: coverage 0.5 < 0.90 -> low_coverage, although the floor -140 would be silent_input.

cases.description: silent_input is evaluated before clipped.
cases.derivation: 99 non-clipped frames at -120 (floor -120 < -110) plus one clipped frame: silent_input outranks clipped.

cases.description: Pre-window check, quiet room.
Pre-window burst boundary: exactly 10.0 dB.
Pre-window burst boundary: 10.1 dB.
Pre-window does not judge stability or absolute loudness (A1-06: the TV judges rise and margin).
cases.derivation: n = 40: idx 0-7 = -28, 8-19 = -24, 20-31 = -20, 32-37 = -16, 38-39 = -15. p20 = sorted[7] = -28, floor = sorted[19] = -24, p80 = sorted[31] = -20, p95 = sorted[37] = -16. p80 - p20 = 8 (would be unstable_floor for a quiet check) and floor -24 > -30 (would be too_loud), but unstable_floor and too_loud do not exist for pre_window: only p95 - floor = 8 <= 10 is checked. Valid.

cases.description: Pre-window coverage boundary: 36 of 40.
cases.derivation: 36 finite frames, expected 40: coverage 0.90 >= 0.90: valid.

cases.description: Pre-window coverage: 35 of 40.
Low coverage is reported before clipped.
cases.derivation: 21 finite frames of 100 expected: coverage 0.21 < 0.90. A clipped frame is also present; low_coverage outranks clipped.

cases.description: Pre-window: a clipped frame invalidates.
cases.derivation: 40 finite frames (coverage 1) of which 1 is clipped: clipped. Statistics use the 39 non-clipped frames at -50.

cases.description: Pre-window: 3 of 40 frames non-finite.
cases.derivation: 37 finite + 3 non-finite: non-finite fraction 3/40 = 0.075 > 0.05: nonfinite. Coverage 37/40 = 0.925 would have passed.

cases.description: Pre-window priority: clipped outranks burst_noise.
cases.derivation: 39 non-clipped frames: sorted idx 0-19 = -50, 20-38 = -30. floor = sorted[ceil(19.5)-1 = 19] = -50, p20 = sorted[7] = -50, p80 = sorted[ceil(31.2)-1 = 31] = -30, p95 = sorted[ceil(37.05)-1 = 37] = -30: p95 - floor = 20 (a burst), but the clipped frame outranks it.
